<!-- All news items below this line -->{{Current events|year=2003|month=11|day=2|content=
* [[American occupation of Iraq|Occupation of Iraq]]: In the heaviest single loss for the coalition troops since cessation of the military campaign in [[Iraq]] two US [[CH-47 Chinook|Chinook]] helicopters are fired on by two [[surface-to-air missile]]s and one crashes near Fallujah and on its way to Baghdad airport; 16 soldiers are killed and 20 wounded.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.reuters.com/newsArticle.jhtml;jsessionid=DWZGY4XS5WOC4CRBAEZSFFA?type=topNews&storyID=3737651 |title=Archived copy |access-date=2017-12-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050630031338/http://www.reuters.com/newsArticle.jhtml |archive-date=2005-06-30 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.cnn.com/2003/WORLD/meast/11/02/sprj.irq.int.main/index.html |title=U.S. helicopter shot down in Iraq - Nov. 2, 2003 |publisher=CNN.com |date=2003-11-02 |accessdate=2015-10-24}}</ref> A blast damages an oil pipeline near [[Kirkuk]], north of Baghdad.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.abc.net.au/news/newsitems/s980590.htm |title=Archived copy |access-date=2017-09-18 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040426131804/http://www.abc.net.au/news/newsitems/s980590.htm |archive-date=2004-04-26 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
* [[War on Terrorism]]: The ''New York Times'' reports that [[Insurgent|militant]] Muslim recruits are "''streaming into [[Iraq]]''" and answering the call of [[Osama bin Laden]] and other extremists. These individuals are joining the fight against the coalition's occupation in Iraq, state counterterrorism officials. Intelligence officials (in six countries) have detected an estimate of hundreds of militant young Muslims from various countries headed for Iraq (primarily by crossing the [[Syria]]n or [[Iran]]ian borders).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.theage.com.au/articles/2003/11/01/1067597202524.html |title=Muslim recruits 'streaming into Iraq' |publisher=www.theage.com.au |date=2003-11-02 |accessdate=2015-10-24}}</ref>
* The [[Yukos]] crisis continues, and [[Dmitry Medvedev]], the new Chief of Staff of the Russian president, warns of risks to the economy.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/business/3234015.stm |title=Business &#124; Kremlin urges caution on Yukos |publisher=BBC News |date=2003-11-02 |accessdate=2015-10-24}}</ref> Following his appointment, the [[silovik]]s continue to dominate Putin's administration in a larger degree than in the [[Boris Yeltsin]] and [[Mikhail Gorbachev]] years.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.themoscowtimes.com/stories/2003/11/03/002.html |title=Archived copy |access-date=2017-09-18 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070914142905/http://www.themoscowtimes.com/stories/2003/11/03/002.html |archive-date=2007-09-14 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
* In the United Kingdom, [[Tony Blair]] faces a formal complaint that has been made to the [[International Criminal Court]] about the prosecution of the Iraq War.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.hindustantimes.com/news/181_443202,0005.htm |title=Archived copy |access-date=2017-09-18 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141016210724/http://www.hindustantimes.com/news/181_443202,0005.htm |archive-date=2014-10-16 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
* In [[Hawaii]], a shark bites the arm off a 13-year-old girl surfing at [[Kauai]], the fourth such amputation in Hawaiian waters in 20 years.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.reuters.com/newsArticle.jhtml;jsessionid=DWZGY4XS5WOC4CRBAEZSFFA?type=domesticNews&storyID=3737032 |title=Archived copy |access-date=2017-12-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050630031338/http://www.reuters.com/newsArticle.jhtml |archive-date=2005-06-30 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
* In the [[Sudan]], [[locust]]s cause breathing difficulties and some deaths in Sudan.<ref>http://interestalert.com/brand/siteia.shtml?Story=st/sn/11010004aaa02aa7.upi&Sys=siteia&Fid=LATEBRKN&Type=News&Filter=Late%20Breaking</ref>
* Former brokers of Prudential Securities are to be charged in Massachusetts as part of a widening investigation into abuses at mutual funds.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.reuters.com/newsArticle.jhtml;jsessionid=DWZGY4XS5WOC4CRBAEZSFFA?type=businessNews&storyID=3737397 |title=Archived copy |access-date=2017-12-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050630031338/http://www.reuters.com/newsArticle.jhtml |archive-date=2005-06-30 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
